answer.generated: In the most recent versions of SQL, the clause used to limit the output to the top 10 rows is referred to as "fetch first 10 rows only" in IBM DB2, and "select top 10 ID, GPA" in Microsoft SQL Server, which differs from the earlier LIMIT clause. Specifically, the fetch clause is integrated into the SELECT statement in IBM DB2, whereas Microsoft SQL Server incorporates the limitation within the SELECT clause using the TOP keyword, thus altering the syntax and placement compared to the traditional LIMIT clause found in earlier versions of SQL.
